question: A 24-year-old woman comes to the clinic because her period is 4 weeks late, and she is experiencing fatigue and morning nausea. She had her last period almost 8 weeks ago. She is gravida 0 para 0 with previously regular menses and an unremarkable medical history. She had her menarche at the age of 13 years. She has a single sexual partner and does not use contraception. At presentation, her vital signs are within normal limits. Gynecological examination reveals breast and uterine enlargement. There is also cyanosis and softening in the cervical and vaginal regions. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.opa: The venous congestion in the patient’s reproductive organs is due to the influence of estrogens
options.opb: Estrone has the largest blood concentration among the estrogens in this patient
options.opc: Hyperestrogenemia is the most probable cause of this patient’s menstrual delay
options.opd: In the patient’s condition, blood estrogen level falls dramatically
options.ope: As the patient’s condition progresses, her estriol levels may rise up to 1000-fold

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Late period and symptoms of fatigue and morning nausea" -> "Possible pregnancy" -> "Increased levels of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)" -> "Stimulation of corpus luteum to produce progesterone" -> "Progesterone maintains the endometrium for pregnancy" -> "Venous congestion in reproductive organs due to progesterone influence" -> "Cyanosis and softening in cervical and vaginal regions" -> "Likely due to increased blood flow and vascular changes in pregnancy" -> "Estrogens also contribute to venous congestion" -> "Estrogens promote breast and uterine enlargement" -> "Estriol levels may rise during pregnancy" -> "Estriol levels may increase significantly, but not necessarily up to 1000-fold" -> "Estriol levels may rise due to placental production" -> "Estriol levels may not increase 1000-fold" -> 80%

analysis: The patient is likely experiencing a normal early pregnancy based on the symptoms described. The venous congestion in the reproductive organs is due to the influence of progesterone and not estrogens. Estradiol is the predominant estrogen during early pregnancy. Hyperestrogenemia is not the most probable cause of menstrual delay in this case. Estrogen levels do not fall dramatically in early pregnancy. Estriol levels do rise significantly during pregnancy, but not up to 1000-fold.
